object.medium: Concerto for three violins, three violas, three cellos and continuo; autograph dedication score, ink on paper
object.description: In March 1721 Johann Sebastian Bach, then Kapellmeister to the small court of Anhalt-Köthen, sent a beautifully copied set of six concertos to Christian Ludwig, Margrave of Brandenburg, with a flattering French dedication. The margrave seems never to have had them played; the score sat in his library and was valued at a few groschen when he died. Today the six are the most celebrated orchestral works of the Baroque. The third concerto, in G major, is written for three violins, three violas, three cellos and continuo, and Bach treats the nine string parts as a single shifting texture, passing figures between the groups in rapid conversation. The page shown here is Bach's own title page from the dedication score, now in the Berlin State Library. The visitor hears the first movement, played by the Advent Chamber Orchestra in a live concert recording from December 2006, released under a Creative Commons licence.
facts: The dedication is dated 24 March 1721; the concertos themselves were probably composed over the preceding years at Köthen and Weimar.
The third concerto has no full slow movement, only two chords linking the two fast movements, which players often expand with a short improvised cadenza.
The dedication score survived in the Berlin Royal Library and is now Am.B. 78 at the Staatsbibliothek zu Berlin.
